html:
The Ten-Day War was a short war in June and July 1991 between Slovenia and the Yugoslav People's Army, fought after Slovenia declared independence on 25 June 1991.

Slovenia, the richest republic of Yugoslavia, had voted for independence in December 1990 after years of quarrels with Belgrade. When the army moved to take the border posts, Slovene territorial defence forces blocked roads and besieged barracks. About 60 to 70 people were killed. The Brioni Agreement ended the fighting, and the army left by October. Slovenia, with almost no Serb minority, got away lightly. It joined the European Union in 2004 and adopted the euro in 2007. The war began the breakup of Yugoslavia.
sum: The Ten-Day War was a short war in June and July 1991 between Slovenia and the Yugoslav People's Army, fought after Slovenia declared independence on 25 June 1991.
